# Set up the environment
```{r}
# ---- Clear the environment ----
rm(list=ls()) # optional

# ---- Load libraries ----
library(readr)

library(tidyr)
library(sf)
library(ggplot2)

# ---- Set file paths ----
```

# Spatial interpolation with IDW
## Load coordinate and shapefile data
```{r}
# ---- Load sample site coordinates ----
site_coord <- read_csv(
  file.path(input_path, "raw/geography/gps_sites_p1-p10.csv"),
  show_col_types = FALSE
)
colnames(site_coord) <- c("Site", "y", "x")
site_coord$Region <- c("Mauka", "Mauka", "Kahawai", "Kahawai", "Kahawai",
                       "Mauka", "Kahawai", "Makai", "Makai", "Mauka")

makaha_coord <- read_csv(
  file.path(input_path, "raw/geography/gps_sites_makaha.csv"),
  show_col_types = FALSE
) %>%
  filter(Site != "RM1") # Remove RM1 (not present in 2014)
colnames(makaha_coord) <- c("Site", "y", "x")

# ---- Join coordinates to metadata ----
meta_xy <- meta %>%
  left_join(site_coord, by = "Site") %>%
  filter(!is.na(x), !is.na(y))

meta_xy <- meta_xy %>%
  mutate(
    Date = if_else(
      Date == as.Date("2014-07-24"),
      as.Date("2014-07-23"),
      Date
    )
  )

# ---- Load shapefiles ----
hfp_total_area  <- read_sf(file.path(input_path, "raw/geography/shape_hfp_2014-2015.shp"))
mangrove_island <- read_sf(file.path(input_path, "raw/geography/shape_mangrove_island.shp"))
hfp_p_sites     <- read_sf(file.path(input_path, "raw/geography/shape_p_site_bounds.shp"))

# ---- Preview geometry ----
ggplot() +
  geom_sf(data = hfp_total_area, fill = NA, color = "black", linewidth = 0.25) +
  geom_sf(data = hfp_p_sites, fill = "grey80", color = "black", linewidth = 0.25) +
  geom_sf(data = mangrove_island, fill = "grey95", color = "black", linewidth = 0.25) +
  geom_point(data = meta_xy, aes(x = x, y = y), size = 1) +
  geom_point(data = makaha_coord, aes(x = x, y = y), size = 2, color = "white", shape = 15) +
  coord_sf()
```

## Calculate interpolations
```{r}
# ---- Lists to iterate over ----
d_list <- c(
  "2014-07-07", # pre-storm
  "2014-07-09",
  "2014-07-14",
  "2014-07-16",
  "2014-07-21", # storm
  "2014-07-23",
  "2014-07-29", # post-storm
  "2014-07-30",
  "2014-08-06",
  "2014-08-11"
)

v_list <- c(
  "S_Temp_C","B_Temp_C",
  "S_Salinity_ppt","B_Salinity_ppt",
  "S_DO_mgL","B_DO_mgL",
  "S_pH","B_pH",
  "tin_t","NO3_uM_t","NO2_uM_t","NH3_uM_t",
  "PO4_uM_t","SiO2_uM_t","Turb_FAU_t",
  "tin_to_tip_t","tin_to_sil_t","sil_to_sal_t"
)

l_list <- c(
  "temp","temp",
  "sal","sal",
  "do","do",
  "ph","ph",
  "logtin","logNO3","logNO2","logNH3",
  "logPO4","logSiO2","logTurb",
  "logtintip","logtinsio2","logsio2sal"
)

# ---- Polygon mask for interpolation ----
mask_poly <- hfp_total_area %>%
  st_make_valid() %>%
  st_union() %>%
  st_as_sf()

# ---- Create interpolation grid ----
cellsize <- 0.000007

grid_sf <- st_make_grid(
  mask_poly,
  cellsize = cellsize,
  what = "centers"
) %>%
  st_as_sf()

grid_sf <- grid_sf[st_within(grid_sf, mask_poly, sparse = FALSE), ]
st_crs(grid_sf) <- 4326

# ---- Interpolation function ----
calc_idw <- function(meta_xy, d, v, l, grid_sf, idp = 2, min_n = 3) {
  df <- meta_xy %>%
    filter(Date == as.Date(d)) %>%
    select(Site, x, y, value = all_of(v)) %>%
    filter(!is.na(value))
  if (nrow(df) < min_n) return(NULL)
  pts_sf <- st_as_sf(df, coords = c("x", "y"), crs = 4326)
  hull <- st_convex_hull(st_union(pts_sf))
  grid_use <- grid_sf[st_within(grid_sf, hull, sparse = FALSE), ]
  if (nrow(grid_use) == 0) return(NULL)
  idw_out <- gstat::idw(
    value ~ 1,
    locations = pts_sf,
    newdata   = grid_use,
    idp       = idp
  )
  idw_out %>%
    mutate(
      d = d,
      v = v,
      quick_ref = l
    )
}

idw_res_list <- list()
k <- 1

for (i in seq_along(v_list)) {
  for (j in seq_along(d_list)) {

    out <- calc_idw(
      meta_xy = meta_xy,
      d = d_list[j],
      v = v_list[i],
      l = l_list[i],
      grid_sf = grid_sf
    )

    if (!is.null(out)) {
      idw_res_list[[k]] <- out
      k <- k + 1
    }
  }
}

idw_res <- bind_rows(idw_res_list)
```

# Plot interpolations
```{r}
# ---- Set latitude and Longitude breaks ----
lat_breaks <- c(21.433, 21.435, 21.437, 21.439) # Latitude breaks (y-axis): °N"
long_breaks <- c(-157.806, -157.808, -157.810) # Longitude breaks (x-axis): °W"

# ---- Plot single panel (one date, one layer, one variable) ----
plot_idw <- function(idw_sf_one, breaks, labels = NULL,
                     linewidth = 0.5) {

  stopifnot(inherits(idw_sf_one, "sf"))
  if (is.null(labels)) labels <- breaks

  lims <- range(c(idw_sf_one$var1.pred, breaks), na.rm = TRUE)

  # Extract coordinates from sf geometry
  xy <- sf::st_coordinates(idw_sf_one)

  df_grid <- idw_sf_one %>%
    sf::st_drop_geometry() %>%
    dplyr::mutate(x = xy[, 1], y = xy[, 2]) %>%
    dplyr::select(x, y, var1.pred)

  # Plot 
  p <- ggplot() +
    
    # Add fishpond border
    geom_sf(data = hfp_total_area, fill = NA, color = "black", linewidth = 0.5) + # Simple feature object
    
    # Add variable color gradient
    geom_raster(data = df_grid, aes(x = x, y = y, fill = var1.pred), interpolate = TRUE) + # Raster object
    
  scale_fill_gradientn(
      colors = rev(RColorBrewer::brewer.pal(11, "Spectral")),
      limits = lims,
      breaks = breaks,
      labels = labels,
      na.value = NA
    ) +
    
    # Add mangrove island
    geom_sf(data = mangrove_island, fill = "grey95", color = "black", linewidth = 0.5) + # Simple feature object
    
    # Coordinate settings
    scale_x_continuous(breaks = long_breaks) + # Longitude
    scale_y_continuous(breaks = lat_breaks) + # Latitude
    
    # Add site points
    geom_point(data = makaha_coord, aes(x = x, y = y), size = 2, color = "white", shape = 18) + # makaha
    geom_point(data = site_coord, aes(x = x, y = y, shape = Region), size = 1.5, color = "black") + # sampling sites
    scale_shape_manual(values = c("Kahawai"= 1, "Makai" = 0, "Mauka" = 2), guide = "none") +
    
    # Other aesthetics
    theme_minimal() +
    theme(
      axis.title = element_blank(),
      axis.text  = element_blank(),
      panel.grid.major = element_blank(),
      panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
      axis.ticks = element_line(linewidth = 0.5),
      axis.ticks.length = unit(6, "pt"),
      plot.margin = margin(0, 0, 0, 0, "cm")
    )
}

# ---- Extract and save legend ----
plot_idw_legend <- function(idw_sf_one, breaks, labels = NULL, title,
                            barheight = 4.5) {

  if (is.null(labels)) labels <- breaks

  # Build a "real" plot (but we will only KEEP the legend)
  p_for_leg <- plot_idw(
    idw_sf_one = idw_sf_one,
    breaks = breaks,
    labels = labels
    ) + 
  
  # Legend aesthetics
    guides(fill = guide_colorbar(
      title = title,
      title.position = "left",
      title.hjust = 0.5,
      label.position = "right",
      barwidth = 0.5,
      barheight = barheight,
      ticks = TRUE,
      ticks.colour = "black",
      ticks.linewidth = 0.5,
      frame.colour = "black",
      frame.linewidth = 0.5
    )) +
    theme(
      legend.position = "right",
      legend.title = element_text(angle = 90, face = "bold", size = 20),
      legend.text  = element_text(size = 20),
      legend.ticks.length = unit(0.5, "mm")
    )

  # Extract ONLY the legend (no plotting panel)
  ggpubr::as_ggplot(ggpubr::get_legend(p_for_leg))
}

# ---- Dates to plot ----
d_list <- c(
  "2014-07-09", # pre-storm
  "2014-07-16",
  "2014-07-23", # storm
  "2014-07-30", # post-storm
  "2014-08-06"
)

# ---- Build the multi-date panel (surface + optional bottom) + legend ----
plot_shm <- function(quick_ref,
                     breaks,
                     labels = NULL,
                     title,
                     n_dates = length(d_list)) {

  df <- idw_res %>% dplyr::filter(quick_ref == !!quick_ref)

  if (nrow(df) == 0) stop("No IDW results found for quick_ref = ", quick_ref)

  # Detect whether this quick_ref includes S_ and B_ layers
  has_S <- any(substr(df$v, 1, 2) == "S_")
  has_B <- any(substr(df$v, 1, 2) == "B_")

  # If no S_/B_ prefix exists (e.g., nutrients), treat as single-layer
  # and label it like "Surface" would have been.
  single_layer <- !(has_S || has_B)

  make_row <- function(layer_prefix = NULL) {
    row_plots <- vector("list", length = n_dates)

    for (k in seq_len(n_dates)) {
      this_date <- d_list[k]

      if (single_layer) {
        one <- df %>% dplyr::filter(d == this_date)
      } else {
        one <- df %>% dplyr::filter(d == this_date, substr(v, 1, 2) == layer_prefix)
      }

      if (nrow(one) == 0) {
        # blank tile if missing
        row_plots[[k]] <- ggplot() + theme_void() + coord_sf()
      } else {
        row_plots[[k]] <- plot_idw(
          idw_sf_one = one,
          breaks = breaks,
          labels = labels,
        ) + theme(legend.position = "none")
      }
    }

    ggpubr::ggarrange(plotlist = row_plots, ncol = n_dates, nrow = 1, align = "hv")
  }

  # Build rows
  p_surface <- make_row("S_")
  p_bottom  <- if (has_B) make_row("B_") else NULL

  # Add left-side labels if we truly have two layers
  if (!single_layer && has_S) {
    p_surface <- ggpubr::annotate_figure(
      p_surface,
      left = ggpubr::text_grob("Surface", rot = 90, vjust = 0.5, size = 20)
    )
  }
  if (!single_layer && has_B) {
    p_bottom <- ggpubr::annotate_figure(
      p_bottom,
      left = ggpubr::text_grob("Bottom", rot = 90, vjust = 0.5, size = 20)
    )
  }

  # Stack rows
  panels_plot <- if (!is.null(p_bottom)) {
    ggpubr::ggarrange(p_surface, p_bottom, ncol = 1, nrow = 2, align = "hv")
  } else {
    p_surface
  }

  # Legend: use first available non-empty slice to set scale + legend
  legend_df <- df %>% dplyr::filter(d == d_list[1])
  if (!single_layer) {
    if (has_S) legend_df <- legend_df %>% dplyr::filter(substr(v, 1, 2) == "S_")
    if (nrow(legend_df) == 0 && has_B) legend_df <- df %>% dplyr::filter(d == d_list[1], substr(v, 1, 2) == "B_")
  }
  if (nrow(legend_df) == 0) legend_df <- df[1, , drop = FALSE]

  barheight <- if (!single_layer && has_B) 9 else 4.5

  legend_plot <- plot_idw_legend(
    idw_sf_one = legend_df,
    breaks = breaks,
    labels = labels,
    title = title,
    barheight = barheight
  )

  list(panels_plot, legend_plot)
}

assemble_panels <- function(plot_list, w = c(1,4)) {
  ggpubr::ggarrange(plot_list[[2]], plot_list[[1]], ncol = 2, widths = w)
}
```

# Supplementary ratio spatial heatmaps
```{r}
# Cap extreme interpolated values for ratios before plotting
idw_res_capped <- idw_res %>%
  mutate(
    var1.pred = case_when(
      # Cap TIN:TIP at 50 mol:mol (ecologically reasonable upper limit)
      quick_ref == "logtintip" & var1.pred > log10(65) ~ log10(65),
      
      # Cap TIN:SiO2 at 16 mol:mol (Redfield ratio)
      quick_ref == "logtinsio2" & var1.pred > log10(17) ~ log10(17),
      
      # Cap SiO2:Sal at 30 μM:ppt (reasonable upper limit)
      quick_ref == "logsio2sal" & var1.pred > log10(31) ~ log10(31),
      
      # Keep all other values as-is
      TRUE ~ var1.pred
    )
  )
```

```{r}
# ---- Unified plot function with color scheme options ----
plot_idw_unified <- function(idw_sf_one, breaks, labels = NULL,
                            color_scheme = "sequential",
                            midpoint = NULL,
                            linewidth = 0.5) {
  
  stopifnot(inherits(idw_sf_one, "sf"))
  if (is.null(labels)) labels <- breaks
  
  lims <- range(c(idw_sf_one$var1.pred, breaks), na.rm = TRUE)
  
  # Extract coordinates from sf geometry
  xy <- sf::st_coordinates(idw_sf_one)
  
  df_grid <- idw_sf_one %>%
    sf::st_drop_geometry() %>%
    dplyr::mutate(x = xy[, 1], y = xy[, 2]) %>%
    dplyr::select(x, y, var1.pred)
  
  # Build base plot
  p <- ggplot() +
    geom_sf(data = hfp_total_area, fill = NA, color = "black", linewidth = 0.5) +
    geom_raster(data = df_grid, aes(x = x, y = y, fill = var1.pred), interpolate = TRUE)
  
  # Add color scale based on scheme
  if (color_scheme == "sequential") {
    # Spectral palette (for main nutrients)
    p <- p + scale_fill_gradientn(
      colors = rev(RColorBrewer::brewer.pal(11, "Spectral")),
      limits = lims,
      breaks = breaks,
      labels = labels,
      na.value = NA
    )
  } else if (color_scheme == "diverging") {
    # Purple-white-green diverging (for ratios with reference point)
    if (is.null(midpoint)) stop("midpoint required for diverging color scheme")
    
    # Use gradientn for full control - position colors manually
    scale_lims <- c(min(breaks), max(breaks))
    
    # Calculate where midpoint falls in the 0-1 range of the scale
    midpoint_position <- (midpoint - scale_lims[1]) / (scale_lims[2] - scale_lims[1])
    
    p <- p + scale_fill_gradientn(
      colors = c("#9970AB", "white", "#5AAE61"),  # purple, white, green
      values = c(0, midpoint_position, 1),  # position white exactly at midpoint
      limits = scale_lims,
      breaks = breaks,
      labels = labels,
      na.value = NA
    )
  } else if (color_scheme == "sequential_diverging") {
    # Purple-white gradient (for uniformly limited ratios)
    p <- p + scale_fill_gradient(
      low = "#9970AB",
      high = "white",
      limits = lims,
      breaks = breaks,
      labels = labels,
      na.value = NA
    )
  }
  
  # Add remaining layers
  p <- p +
    geom_sf(data = mangrove_island, fill = "grey95", color = "black", linewidth = 0.5) +
    scale_x_continuous(breaks = long_breaks) +
    scale_y_continuous(breaks = lat_breaks) +
    geom_point(data = makaha_coord, aes(x = x, y = y), size = 2, color = "white", shape = 18) +
    geom_point(data = site_coord, aes(x = x, y = y, shape = Region), size = 1.5, color = "black") +
    scale_shape_manual(values = c("Kahawai"= 1, "Makai" = 0, "Mauka" = 2), guide = "none") +
    theme_minimal() +
    theme(
      axis.title = element_blank(),
      axis.text  = element_blank(),
      panel.grid.major = element_blank(),
      panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
      axis.ticks = element_line(linewidth = 0.5),
      axis.ticks.length = unit(6, "pt"),
      plot.margin = margin(0, 0, 0, 0, "cm")
    )
  
  return(p)
}

# ---- Unified legend function ----
plot_idw_legend_unified <- function(idw_sf_one, breaks, labels = NULL, 
                                   title, color_scheme = "sequential",
                                   midpoint = NULL, barheight = 4.5) {
  
  if (is.null(labels)) labels <- breaks
  
  p_for_leg <- plot_idw_unified(
    idw_sf_one = idw_sf_one,
    breaks = breaks,
    labels = labels,
    color_scheme = color_scheme,
    midpoint = midpoint
  ) + 
    guides(fill = guide_colorbar(
      title = title,
      title.position = "left",
      title.hjust = 0.5,
      label.position = "right",
      barwidth = 0.5,
      barheight = barheight,
      ticks = TRUE,
      ticks.colour = "black",
      ticks.linewidth = 0.5,
      frame.colour = "black",
      frame.linewidth = 0.5
    )) +
    theme(
      legend.position = "right",
      legend.title = element_text(angle = 90, face = "bold", size = 20),
      legend.text  = element_text(size = 20),
      legend.ticks.length = unit(0.5, "mm")
    )
  
  ggpubr::as_ggplot(ggpubr::get_legend(p_for_leg))
}

# ---- Unified multi-panel function ----
plot_shm_unified <- function(quick_ref,
                            breaks,
                            labels = NULL,
                            title,
                            color_scheme = "sequential",
                            midpoint = NULL,
                            n_dates = length(d_list)) {
  
  df <- idw_res_capped %>% dplyr::filter(quick_ref == !!quick_ref)
  
  if (nrow(df) == 0) stop("No IDW results found for quick_ref = ", quick_ref)
  
  # Build row of panels
  row_plots <- vector("list", length = n_dates)
  
  for (k in seq_len(n_dates)) {
    this_date <- d_list[k]
    one <- df %>% dplyr::filter(d == this_date)
    
    if (nrow(one) == 0) {
      row_plots[[k]] <- ggplot() + theme_void()
    } else {
      row_plots[[k]] <- plot_idw_unified(
        idw_sf_one = one,
        breaks = breaks,
        labels = labels,
        color_scheme = color_scheme,
        midpoint = midpoint
      ) + theme(legend.position = "none")
    }
  }
  
  panels_plot <- ggpubr::ggarrange(plotlist = row_plots, ncol = n_dates, nrow = 1, align = "hv")
  
  # Legend
  legend_df <- df %>% dplyr::filter(d == d_list[1])
  if (nrow(legend_df) == 0) legend_df <- df[1, , drop = FALSE]
  
  legend_plot <- plot_idw_legend_unified(
    idw_sf_one = legend_df,
    breaks = breaks,
    labels = labels,
    title = title,
    color_scheme = color_scheme,
    midpoint = midpoint,
    barheight = 4.5
  )
  
  list(panels_plot, legend_plot)
}

# TIN:TIP - diverging scale with symmetric limits
shm_tintip <- plot_shm_unified(
  quick_ref = "logtintip",
  breaks = c(log10(1), log10(5), log10(17), log10(65)),
  labels = c("0", "4", "16", "64+"),
  title = expression(bold("TIN:TIP")),
  color_scheme = "diverging",
  midpoint = log10(17)
); (shm_tintip_w_leg <- assemble_panels(shm_tintip, w = c(1.1, 4)))

# TIN:SiO2 - purple to white gradient (white = 1:1 Redfield ratio)
shm_tinsio2 <- plot_shm_unified(
  quick_ref = "logtinsio2",
  breaks = c(log10(1), log10(1.4), log10(2)),
  labels = c("0", "0.4", "1"),
  title = expression(bold("TIN:SiO"[2])),
  color_scheme = "sequential_diverging",  # Purple to white only
  midpoint = NULL  # Not needed for sequential_diverging
); (shm_tinsio2_w_leg <- assemble_panels(shm_tinsio2, w = c(1.1, 4)))

# Calculate mid-range for SiO2:Sal (for centering)
sio2sal_midrange <- meta_xy %>%
  filter(Date %in% as.Date(c("2014-07-09", "2014-07-16", "2014-07-23", 
                             "2014-07-30", "2014-08-06"))) %>%
  summarize(
    min_val = min(sil_to_sal_t, na.rm = TRUE),
    max_val = max(sil_to_sal_t, na.rm = TRUE),
    midrange = (min_val + max_val) / 2
  ) %>%
  pull(midrange)

# SiO2:Sal - diverging scale centered at mean
shm_sio2sal <- plot_shm_unified(
  quick_ref = "logsio2sal",
  breaks = c(log10(1.3), log10(4), log10(11), log10(31)),
  labels = c("0.3", "3", "10", "30+"),
  title = expression(bold("SiO"[2]*":Sal")),
  color_scheme = "diverging",
  midpoint = sio2sal_midrange
); (shm_sio2sal_w_leg <- assemble_panels(shm_sio2sal, w = c(1.1, 4)))
```

# Summary of spatial interpolation

**Plain-language summary**
To visualize how water quality varied across the fishpond, we created interpolated maps for each sampling date. We used inverse distance weighting (IDW), a method that estimates values at unsampled locations by giving more weight to nearby measurements than to distant ones. Interpolation was constrained to the area enclosed by our sampling sites to avoid extrapolating beyond the data. This produced smooth spatial surfaces that reveal gradients and patterns across the fishpond while remaining faithful to the observed measurements.

**Publication-ready summary**
Continuous spatial surfaces were generated for each physicochemical variable and sampling date using inverse distance weighting (IDW; power = 2). Interpolation was performed on a regular grid and constrained to the convex hull of sampling locations to prevent extrapolation beyond observed data.
